analysis.title: Global Rates Weekly: Fright to quality
key_insights: BofA keeps a bear flattening bias in US rates into payrolls and the Nov 4 refunding. Above-trend growth and above-target inflation are expected to dominate oil and equity-driven curve volatility.

The Oct FOMC held rates as widely expected, with Governor Cook's dissent a surprise. The press conference drove the market move: from its start the 2Y rate fell 6bp and the 30Y rate rose 4bp. BofA reads the sharp 2s30s steepening as doubt over Warsh's inflation-fighting credibility, similar to the July FOMC.

US economists now expect 25bp Fed hikes in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027 (previously earlier timing, same terminal level). BofA leaves its UST forecasts unchanged, with the 10Y at 5.00% at YE26 and Fed funds at 4.375%.

Higher long-end yields raise the odds that Treasury cuts long-end auction sizes, possibly at the Nov 4 refunding. The buyback tool is spent. Traditional long-end buyers (insurers, pensions) hold about 6.5% of non-bill UST supply, near the lowest since the early 1950s, while 10Y+ issuance share has grown since the mid-2010s.

BofA stays paid 2Y UST and in 2s30s flatteners, and long 30Y and 2Y asset swap spreads. Risks to the 2Y pay view are the dovish Fed, soft tech earnings (GOOG and AMZN investment scrutiny, MSFT ROI still rewarded) and 2Y/5Y yields near CTA short-cover levels.

Week ahead in the US: ISM manufacturing Monday, mid-term elections Tuesday, refunding and ISM services Wednesday, payrolls Friday. BofA expects Oct NFP at 75k (consensus 65k) and unemployment at 4.2%, which would modestly bear flatten the curve. A Democratic win would bull steepen with regulatory and tax risk, a Republican win would bear flatten with easier fiscal policy.

Repo rates are rising into Oct month-end on a higher TGA, heavy bill issuance and the Canadian year-end. BofA expects the Fed to restart reserve management purchases (RMPs) in mid-Nov at about $10b a month, and repo to stabilize after month-end. This supports its long Dec 2026 SOFR/FF trade.

ECB held rates with a dovish statement (underlying inflation and wages behaving, downside growth risk from energy and financing conditions, 'measured approach') but Lagarde repeated a December hiking bias. Markets priced out about 3bp of 74bp of hikes over the next year. BofA expects one final hike in December, with cuts from Sep 2027.

Lagarde offered only verbal intervention on French spreads and did not signal flexibility on full QT. BofA reads the pain threshold for balance sheet action as still high. It expects 10y OAT-Bund spreads to follow global risk assets with a near-term tightening bias, helped by Moody's leaving France's rating unchanged.

In EUR rates BofA leans bullish duration and prefers owning the belly over the front end. Over the past month 75% of 2s10s moves were led by the 10Y, and 1y and 1y1y OIS traded in a range under 10bp despite higher oil and gas prices.

UK: the market fully prices a 25bp BoE hike next week and more than two further hikes. BofA expects a dovish hike from 3.75% to 4.0% on a 7-2 vote, which could bull flatten the MPC curve. It enters a receive June 2027 MPC-dated Sonia trade and keeps its 1y forward 2s10s Sonia steepener.

The UK Autumn Budget remit raised net financing for 2026-27 by £7.4bn to £258.6bn and cut the long-dated Gilt share to 6%. BofA still sees long Gilt sales as challenging, with more than £10bn of longs to sell in five months and indigestion risk in 1Q27. The Gilt curve bull flattened on the day.

Australia: the RBA is expected to hike to 4.85% on Tuesday after Q3 trimmed mean CPI of 1.0% q/q beat its forecast. BofA sees this as the cycle peak and closed its 2s10s flattener at 26bp, short of its 10bp target, on dovish press conference risk and softening domestic data.

Japan: 30Y JGBs have fallen below 4% and PCA shows the rally was broad-based, with relative cheapness now in the 40-year sector. BofA suggests taking profits on some RV positions (long JL197/short JL195, long JX91/short JX89) and keeping 30s40s flatteners via long JU19 or JU18 against short JX91.

Canada: the BoC hiked 25bp to 2.50%, its first hike in over three years, against BofA's call for a hold at 2.25%. BofA now expects one more hike in January and sees the hawkish BoC as supportive of a flatter CA curve versus the US. It enters a 5s30s CA flattener versus US steepener at a 30bp spread.

Euro inflation: the real €str 2s10s curve is priced to flatten 75bp over a year, from 91bp to 16bp. BofA keeps its 1y forward 2s10s real steepener (now 19bp, entered at 10bp) and its BTPei 2030/33/36 barbell, which is at 15.4bp against a 13bp target. About €100bn of short-dated linkers leave sub-1y indices between July and May, which BofA sees as supportive for longer real yields.

Technicals: the US 10Y yield is in an uptrend from the March 2026 low, and the decline from the 5.36% YTD high looks corrective. BofA favors fading a move toward 4.83% (rising trend line) and keeps a pay-rates bias unless yield falls firmly below 4.74%.

Central bank hike pricing by YE26 is more hawkish than BofA forecasts in the UK and Canada. BofA expects Fed 2 more hikes, ECB 1 more, BoE 2 (Nov-26 and Feb-27) then cuts by 2028, BoJ a Dec hike, BoC 1 in Jan 2027, and no more RBA hikes in its base case.
earnings_insights: Late-week soft tech earnings drew greater scrutiny of investment plans at GOOG and AMZN, while MSFT's ROI was still rewarded. BofA calls this a headwind to its pay 2Y UST view. No EPS or revenue figures are given.

Unchanged rate alongside above-consensus payrolls reinforces the strong-data, sticky-inflation view.

BofA considers the BoC's 3.5% year-end inflation forecast too high against this reading, which is part of why it expects a January hike rather than December.
Above the RBA's August forecast. Led BofA economists to forecast a November RBA hike to 4.85%.
BofA sees a fifth hike this year as the peak and closed its AU 2s10s flattener.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Expected not to be market moving.
BofA expects a dovish hike that bull flattens the MPC curve. The market prices a further 10bp by December and more than two additional hikes.

macro_indicators.reading: 22bp implied vs 21bp before the statement, 74bp over the coming year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Lagarde's repeated hiking bias undid part of the initial dovish reaction. BofA expects a final hike in December.
Below the 5.36% YTD high. BofA's YE26 forecast is 5.00% and it favors paying on dips.

risk_factors: A surprisingly hawkish Fed would hurt the CA-versus-US flattener and the US steepener legs.
A dovish Fed pivot or Treasury stops long-end support would hurt the 2s30s flattener and the 2Y pay view.
Equity selloff and poor long-end liquidity are risks to the long 10y20y inflation swap.
Material fiscal slippage in the UK and long Gilt supply indigestion in 1Q27.
No Fed RMP restart would hurt the Dec 2026 SOFR/FF trade.
French budget and election uncertainty with year-end risk constraints keep BofA cautious on OATs.
Energy price moves could change ECB and BoC paths. A collapse in energy prices could break the December ECB hike.
A hawkish BoE hike or hawkish RBA press conference or NAIRU revision.
Rising leverage in markets via CTA short covering in 2Y and 5Y USTs.
charts_described: Exhibit 5 shows 2s30s curve changes under the Warsh Fed, with large moves on the June, July, Sept and Oct FOMC days and Jackson Hole versus other days.
Exhibit 9 shows 75% of 2s10s moves over the past month led by the 10Y in the EUR curve.
Exhibit 10 shows 1y and 1y1y EUR OIS in the tightest range (<10bp) in October versus September.
Exhibit 22 table shows Fed T-bill purchases and net bill supply net of Fed purchases of $97b in Nov and -$195b in Dec 2026, with TGA falling to $850b at YE.
Exhibit 25 notes the real €str 2s10s curve is priced to flatten 75bp over a year, from 91bp to 16bp.
vol_and_positioning: BofA keeps a long forward vol bias in the US (short left versus right side vol), 2s10s floor ladders and 15m1y versus 3m1y receiver calendars.
US 2Y and 5Y yields are near the CTA short-cover trigger ranges after Thursday's rally, so CTA shorts are at risk of covering.
EUR vol is expected to stay supported into YE26 on ECB uncertainty and fall in 2027, via a long 3m2y receiver 1x2.
JP vol is supported and outperforming other developed markets (short 6m1y payer 1x2). AU vol is supported near term and lower in the medium term.

The EUR front end was in its tightest range this year in October: 1y and 1y1y OIS stayed within 10bp. On oil up days the 2y swap rise was smaller than the fall on oil down days (ratio about 0.8 versus 1.6 in Mar-Sep).
Bloomberg's BOEspeak model puts BoE communication at its most hawkish since early 2023.
geopolitical: US mid-term elections on Tuesday, with the market expecting Democrats to win the House and Senate.
Elevated energy prices are cited by the ECB, BoC and RBA as an inflation risk.
New US tariffs cited by the BoC as adding uncertainty to the growth outlook.
French politics: the budget possibly passing by ordonnance, and a long wait until election manifestos and the election itself.
cross_bank_references: Reuters report citing ECB sources that a December hike was all but certain, barring a collapse in energy prices, and that a pause is expected after December.

tension_points.bull_case: A Fed seen as credible on inflation would keep long-end yields anchored, but BofA sees this as the bearish case for the curve: the Oct FOMC press conference steepened 2s30s, as in July under Warsh. BofA expects more hikes (Dec and Mar), flattening the curve and keeping front-end yields higher.
tension_points.bear_case: A dovish Fed pivot and Treasury stopping long-end support, plus a dovish Fed and soft tech earnings, would reverse the pay 2Y and flattener views. Tech earnings and CTA short covering near 2Y/5Y trigger levels are additional risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Short 2Y UST stop at 4.45% and 2s30s flattener stop at 100bp.

tension_points.bull_case: A dovish 25bp hike on a 7-2 vote with limited, gradual further tightening would bull flatten the MPC curve, as in May 2023, favoring receiving June 2027 Sonia.
tension_points.bear_case: Market pricing of more than two further hikes, hawkish BoE communication, a stronger economy and rising energy prices would support a third quarterly hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: June 2027 MPC-dated Sonia rising to the 4.86% stop on a hawkish hike.

tension_points.bull_case: Dovish statement, tight financial conditions, weak second-round effects and ECB source reports of a pause after December support owning duration in the belly.
tension_points.bear_case: Lagarde's repeated hiking bias and elevated energy prices limit front-end rallies.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy price collapse would break the December hike. Resilient growth would hurt the real €str steepener, with its stop at -10bp.

theme_stances.key_argument: A Fed slow to respond to strong activity and elevated inflation raises the risk of more hikes, supporting higher front-end yields and a flatter curve over time.
theme_stances.evidence: The long end may continue to haunt Warsh and the Fed

theme_stances.key_argument: Traditional long-end buyers have shrunk while 10Y+ issuance share has grown, so Treasury is likely to cut long-end auction sizes.
theme_stances.evidence: We have long believed UST should cut long end sizes due to oversupply

theme_stances.key_argument: Markets are pricing too many hikes against tight financial conditions and weak second-round effects, so BofA leans bullish duration in the belly.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to lean bullish duration in EUR
